tasks.short: Collaborate on integrated building and landscape design

steps.what: Collaborate with architects on whole building design, aesthetics, landscape relationships and energy trade-offs

tasks.design: Retain interdisciplinary design collaboration using shared views in the {OTHER} building and landscape design environment and decisions recorded in {DOCS}. The landscape architect and building architect reconcile aesthetics, site relationships and energy implications rather than delegating design agreement to a generator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Whole-building trade-offs depend on project context and the intentions of several disciplines.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared digital views support discussion, but their availability does not establish a new saving in collaborative design time.
tasks.still_hard: Improving one aspect of the design can undermine another, and not all objectives share a useful numerical measure.
tasks.human_edge: The landscape architect understands place, design intent and how to reach a workable agreement with other disciplines.
tasks.altitude: Collaboration effort and design responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Reconcile building form with landscape and energy objectives

evidence.claim: Retaining interdisciplinary design collaboration is a model-knowledge boundary; shared design information alone does not prove reduced collaboration time.

assumptions: Boundary is collaborative design reasoning and agreement, not separate drawing preparation or certified energy calculations.

Building designers produce their proposals, site specialists provide observations and participants create new design alternatives during s1. Interpretation, enquiries and decision capture remain fully counted.
No ready aesthetic-quality or energy-efficient flag is presumed. Missing information returns to manual discussion or separate specialist analysis.
Test native shared-view functions before custom code. OTHER denotes building and landscape design software.
No new integration, capture obligation or automation is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero and existing model runtime earns no saving.
unknowns: Which energy assessments are performed by specialists
research_questions: Which design disagreements require direct collaboration rather than additional data display?

already_counted.description: Design discussion, interpretation and agreement capture

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and incremental=0. Whole-building design collaboration keeps its full time; separate document preparation is not invented within this task.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare graphical design views with configured drawing layouts

steps.what: Develop proposed plans and choose geometry, graphic content, scale and drawing presentation requirements
Prepare graphic representations and drawings by arranging model views, legends and sheet references
Check graphical clarity and consistency with the intended design, then issue the accepted drawing set

tasks.design: Configure view and sheet templates in the {OTHER} landscape drawing environment from the architect's source model and presentation specification. Store the draft in {DOCS}; the architect checks that it communicates the intended design before issuing the exact accepted drawing set.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated view arrangement and sheet references required manual preparation after the substantive design was established.
tasks.enabler_now: Native drawing templates can reuse model views, scales and legends without generating new design geometry.
tasks.still_hard: An accurately plotted view can still be confusing, omit design intent or use an inappropriate level of detail.
tasks.human_edge: The architect chooses what a viewer must understand and recognises misleading graphical emphasis.
tasks.altitude: Repeated sheet preparation may fall; design authorship and issue responsibility stay with the architect.

evidence.claim: Configured drawing views and sheet templates are a model-knowledge design; no measured landscape drawing preparation saving is supplied by the digest.

assumptions: Boundary includes design geometry, graphical preparation and drawing issue; physical site surveying is separate and receives no saving.

The architect produces the model and sheet specification in fully retained s1, including geometry version, view extents, scales, layers, legend choices, sheet ids and intended audience. No ready graphic-complete flag is presumed.
s2 uses only that model and specification. Missing geometry or ambiguous layout choices return to manual work in s1; bespoke illustrations without reusable views remain manually prepared.
Test native drawing configuration before custom code. OTHER denotes landscape drawing and model software. Savings concern repeated manual layout work, not existing plotting runtime.
All graphical meaning checks remain in s3; template maintenance and cross-disciplinary clarification have explicit upkeep allowances.
unknowns: Whether view and sheet preparation is already configured
research_questions: Can native sheet templates reduce repeated preparation without increasing drawing clarity corrections?

already_counted.description: Create geometry and capture presentation requirements
Check graphical meaning and approve issue

incremental.description: Maintain view templates, legends and sheet mappings
Project colleagues clarify changed drawing references

approvals.approved_version: Exact drawing set version, source model version, sheet list and recipients checked in s3; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=65; gross 35 minus 7 focal upkeep gives central net 28. Range covers already-configured layouts and modest reuse across repeated sheets; geometry creation and graphical acceptance retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Coordinate project costing, plans and contractor bids with estimators

steps.what: Collaborate with estimators to clarify project scope, quantities, plans and contractor bid assumptions
Create project cost comparisons and bid schedules from the checked scope and prices
Review costing differences, agree planning implications and coordinate checked clarification requests with contractors

tasks.design: Configure bid comparison and cost-schedule templates in {SPREADSHEET}, using scope and prices checked with the estimator. Keep project implications in {PROJECT}; the architect interprets differences and checks each clarification before sending it through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated comparison preparation mixed arithmetic and copying with substantive commercial and scope clarification.
tasks.enabler_now: Native templates can arrange checked quantities, prices and dates without interpreting contractual exceptions.
tasks.still_hard: Bids may price different scope, omit work or depend on incompatible programme assumptions.
tasks.human_edge: The architect and estimator recognise when an apparent price difference is actually a design or scope difference.
tasks.altitude: Less copying leaves negotiations, scope decisions and project planning with people.

reach.task: Reconcile bid scope and quantify exclusions
reach.learn: Comparable pricing bases and programme dependencies

evidence.claim: Configured bid comparison templates can arrange checked quantities, prices and schedule dates; this is a model-knowledge design with no measured landscape procurement saving in the digest.

assumptions: Boundary is architect collaboration and comparison preparation, not estimator quantity take-off, contractor estimating or contract award. Those roles' existing work receives no focal saving.

Estimators produce quantities and contractors produce bids. In fully retained s1 the architect reconciles and captures item id, description, quantity, unit, price, currency, exclusions, proposed dates, bid version and comparison basis with the estimator.

s2 reads only those checked inputs and the layout. Free-text exclusions are captured and interpreted manually in s1 and s3; no ready comparable-bid code is assumed. Missing details return to manual enquiries rather than invented values.
Contractor clarification responses are produced after s3 sends requests and are captured in a subsequent s1 cycle; they are not an input available before sending.

Test native spreadsheet and project templates before custom code. Additional estimator clarification and template maintenance receive explicit allowances; automatic arithmetic runtime earns no labour saving.
unknowns: How much comparison preparation belongs to the architect
research_questions: Can a checked comparison template reduce copying while keeping scope exclusions and date assumptions visible?

already_counted.description: Scope clarification and capture of checked comparison fields
Interpret differences and check contractor communication

incremental.description: Maintain comparison mappings and project templates
Estimator resolves additional format and scope ambiguities

approvals.approved_version: Exact cost comparison, bid versions, clarification text and contractor recipients checked in s3; changes require renewed checking

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=75; gross 25 minus 8 focal upkeep gives central net 17. Range covers an already-configured comparison and small reductions in repeated copying; collaboration and scope judgement retain all their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Design landscapes to reduce water consumption

steps.what: Create landscapes with site-appropriate planting and water strategies through ecological and aesthetic design judgement

tasks.design: Retain ecological and aesthetic design with the landscape architect using {DOCS} and the {OTHER} landscape design environment. The architect interprets site conditions and plant evidence to choose a coherent water strategy; software does not establish plant suitability or guarantee water savings.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plant performance and water use depend on soil, exposure, establishment and maintenance as well as species choice.
tasks.enabler_now: Design tools can organise information, but the supplied digest provides no demonstrated replacement for this site-specific design judgement.
tasks.still_hard: A drought-tolerant label does not establish suitability for the actual soil, climate or maintenance regime.
tasks.human_edge: The architect combines ecological evidence, place and maintenance reality into a workable landscape.
tasks.altitude: Design effort and responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Assess plant suitability for site conditions and habitat objectives
reach.learn: Limits of generic drought and indigenous-plant labels

evidence.claim: Retaining site-specific planting and water strategy design is a model-knowledge boundary; general mapping or model-query tools do not establish landscape water savings.

assumptions: Boundary is substantive landscape design, not separate drawing layout, irrigation installation or subsequent maintenance. Reused drawing actions must be counted once elsewhere.

Site specialists provide observations and plant sources provide descriptive evidence. The architect captures and interprets soil, exposure, water availability, establishment needs and maintenance assumptions within fully counted s1.
No structured suitable-plant or water-saving flag is presumed. Missing or conflicting evidence leads to manual site enquiries and design revision.
Test existing landscape design functions before custom code. OTHER denotes landscape design software.
No new automation, integration or capture obligation is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero; no environmental outcome number is invented.
unknowns: Availability of representative plant performance evidence
research_questions: Which water assumptions depend on establishment and maintenance rather than species labels?

already_counted.description: Site interpretation and landscape design reasoning

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net zero with no added upkeep. Site-specific planting and water design retain full time; routine drawing generation is outside this boundary.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Repeated drawings and cost comparisons may need less preparation; design collaboration, ecological judgement and external issue responsibility stay with the architect.
reach: Learn site performance limits with ecologists
role.ambitious_version: A landscape architect who can connect design intent, site evidence and transparent project assumptions.
